messages:
incident-bot: HIGH ALERT — streaming decode p99 spike detected (service=decode-serving, region=us-west1). p99=3.25s, p95=1.1s, increased error retry rate. triggered at 2026-03-14T21:47:14Z. dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/streaming/latency

maria: seeing the same in prod traces. tail requests are stalling in decode stage, stacks point to kernel syscalls hanging on pagefaults. p95 jumped around 21:40Z.

jun: this aligns with the TRT/FlashAttention kernel roll from yesterday — build tag trt8-flashattn-20260313 (sha: a1b2c3d). I can see increased page fault counts in the node logs.

laura: we promoted that kernel to canary and then to all during the afternoon to reduce mem copies. we didn't catch the tail behavior in perf runs.

ashok: taking oncall. first pass: is rollback to previous kernel possible without infra downtime?

sre-ops: rollback path exists per runbook. we can pin nodes to kernel v20260308 (pre-flashattn). steps: 1) add node label patch-roll, 2) drain one pool at a time, 3) apply kernel image, 4) uncordon. ops estimate 8-12m per pool.

maria: for immediate mitigation can we toggle the new compile flags that enable aggressive memory prefetch in the decode path? in dev they reduced p50 but increased page faults.

jun: yes, compile flag is NEW_PREFETCH=1. setting to 0 should revert to conservative path. we have a hotpatch script:

```bash
./hotpatch-compile-flags --service decode-serving --set NEW_PREFETCH=0 --confirm
```

laura: careful — that requires an in-service JIT recompile; some models may transiently increase latency. but likely faster than full kernel rollback.

ashok: plan: 1) run hotpatch on one AZ as test (us-west1-a) 2) monitor p99 for 5m 3) if improves, roll to other AZs 4) parallel prepare kernel rollback if hotpatch fails.

product-ops: customer impact — preliminary: 2.4% of streaming sessions saw degraded p99; we surface 3 paying customers with significant fetch rates (AcmeHealth, BrightEdu, Bankly). I opened incident ticket INC-2026-324.

sre-ops: kicked off hotpatch against us-west1-a now. logs: /var/log/hotpatch/decode-20260314.log — tail shows flag toggled.

incident-bot: ACTION_STARTED hotpatch-run by jun at 2026-03-14T21:51:00Z.

maria: after ~90s we see p99 drop from 3.25s -> 1.05s in the canary AZ, error retries down. traces show fewer pagefault spikes.

ashok: good signal. rolling hotpatch to us-west1-b and c next. continue monitoring dashboards and slow query traces. if any customer reports errors escalate immediately.

laura: prepping kernel rollback playbook in parallel in case we see tail regressions reappear after wider rollout. tracker: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/OPS-7421

oncall-bot: HANDOFF scheduled to @ashok for next shift at 2026-03-14T22:15Z. summary: hotpatch toggled NEW_PREFETCH=0; canary p99 improved. kernel rollback ready as fallback. affected customers notified.

ashok: documenting postmortem notes in the incident doc and will follow up with eng-runtime to run longer tail sensitivity tests on the flashattn kernel. tagging runtime and ml infra.

product-ops: notifying impacted customers with brief RCA and mitigation steps, offering priority support.

incident-bot: INCIDENT_STATUS update — mitigation in progress, impact reduced. will mark RESOLVED after 1h of stable p99 below 1.2s.

maria: ongoing: add a perf test that exercises long-sequence streaming tails under flashattn kernel to catch this next time.

jun: noted. I'll create a smoketest job and disable NEW_PREFETCH by default until we validate on larger tail sets.

ashok: handing off to night oncall with status pinned. leaving followups: run kernel bisect on a1b2c3d, add kernel e2e tail tests, postmortem.

oncall-bot: THREAD ANNOTATION — responders: maria, jun, laura, ashok, sre-ops, product-ops. logs and artifacts uploaded to /incidents/2026-03-14/4767001234/

incident-bot: CLOSED? not yet — monitoring continues.
